Yellow Face from the Suffering of People

"Feeling the Sorrow of Others" in a Tale by Saadi

In the story of the Damascus famine, Saadi speaks of a man who is not himself in financial hardship, yet the suffering of the hungry robs him of pleasure. Can one, in times of war, economic hardship, and insecurity, both worry about the suffering of others and continue living?

In this episode, inspired by Saadi's tale, we explore the meaning of empathy in difficult days; we speak about the necessity of compassion and reducing the suffering of others, and we reflect on how the flood of images of suffering on social media can gradually desensitize us. In this segment, we will also seek answers to these questions: Is happiness in times of hardship a sign of indifference, and how can discontent become a criterion for judging others?
